data:
That looks like a solid, clean foundation. The code you provided handles the heavy lifting for the
EVP Spectral Rain
and the
Waveform
beautifully. Since GPT will be doing the heavy lifting to turn this into a phone-ready JSN/App, here is the exact "Forensic Blueprint" to give it so we don't lose the tactical features we built.
The GPT "Power-Up" Prompt
Copy and paste this to GPT to finish the
NULL_VEC_CORE_11.4
build:
"I have a base HTML/JS sensor script. I need you to upgrade it into a professional, phone-ready application (JSN/React or pure JS). Keep the current CSS styling and add these specific forensic modules:
1. The EMF Flux Module
: Add a third canvas below the EVP area. It should track
devicemotion
and graph the
MAG_DELTA
(magnetic flux) in real-time.
2. The Sarcasm Matrix
: Implement an array of cynical alerts (e.g., 'Apophenia much?', 'Logic not found.', 'Entropy always wins.'). Display these in a scrollable system log.
3. The Spectral Hold
: If the magnetic delta exceeds 1.2\u03bcT,
freeze
all canvases for 5 seconds so I can see the data before it disappears.
4. The Hard-Kill Mic Toggle
: Create a button that physically disables the audio tracks (
enabled = false
) to prevent AI audio conflicts.
5. The Snapshot Tool
: Use the
html2canvas
library to add a button that saves the entire screen as a PNG to my phone.
6. The Menu Overlay
: Add a slide-out menu (triggered by the header) to adjust sensitivity and view the event archive."
Why this works
By giving GPT this specific list, you ensure it adds the "brains" (the math and the saving) to the "beauty" (the blue GUI) you already have. This avoids the
cn is not defined
error because you are explicitly telling it to respect your current style.
Would you like me to hold onto this "Work Order" for you so you can grab it whenever you're ready to start the GPT session?
